bodyHtml:
The Katy Painter Homeowners Recommend to Their Neighbors

Katy is master-planned communities, HOA architectural review, and homes that are mostly ten to twenty-five years old. Painting here is rarely about rescuing a neglected house. It is about replacing thin builder-grade finishes, keeping south- and west-facing elevations ahead of the Texas sun, and getting it done with a crew that shows up when it says it will.

The Proud Paintbrush handles interior painting, exterior painting, cabinet painting, drywall repair, and fence staining throughout Katy, with the same prep standards, Sherwin-Williams products, and 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty we use across Fort Bend County.

Recent Katy Project: Cinco Ranch Kitchen Cabinets

This Cinco Ranch kitchen started with dark stained wood cabinets and a matching island. We labeled and removed every door and drawer front, degreased and sanded each surface, applied a bonding primer, and sprayed a hard cabinet enamel for a factory-smooth white finish. The boxes were structurally sound, so the homeowners got a new-looking kitchen without the tear-out, cost, and downtime of replacement.

See more of the process on our cabinet painting in Katy page.

Who We Work With in Katy

  • Homeowners in HOA communities like Cinco Ranch, Cane Island, and Falcon Point who need exterior colors approved before work starts

  • Families upgrading scuffed, flat builder paint to a finish that wipes clean

  • Owners of brick and Hardie siding homes whose trim, soffits, and siding are showing sun fade

  • People who want one written scope, one schedule, and one person accountable from estimate to final walkthrough

Our Painting Process in Katy

  1. Walk the home together and agree on scope — one room, a full interior, cabinets, or the exterior

  2. Identify repairs upfront: nail pops, settling cracks, failed caulk, and soft trim

  3. Prepare HOA color submissions where your community requires them

  4. Protect floors, furniture, and landscaping, and keep the job site clean every day

  5. Walk the finished work with you before we call the job complete

The Proud Paintbrush is based in Sugar Land, locally owned since 2020, and Fully Insured · $1M Liability. Read what to expect during your project, compare our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty, or explore all of our service areas.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to hire house painters in Katy, TX?
faqs.a: Most Katy projects land between $2,500 and $20,000+ depending on home size, surfaces, and prep. A single room or cabinet refresh sits at the low end; a full two-story exterior sits at the high end. Every project is quoted in writing after a free on-site walkthrough. See our pricing page for detailed ranges by service.

faqs.q: Do you handle HOA color approval in Katy?
faqs.a: Yes. Cinco Ranch, Cane Island, Falcon Point, and most other Katy communities require architectural approval for exterior color changes. We help prepare the color codes, product specs, and photos your HOA asks for and build the approval time into your schedule.

faqs.q: When should a newer Katy home be repainted?
faqs.a: Many Katy homeowners repaint interiors within a few years of move-in to replace flat builder-grade paint that scuffs and won't wipe clean. Exteriors typically need trim, soffits, and siding repainted every 7 to 10 years, sooner on south- and west-facing sides.

faqs.q: Why do Katy homes get nail pops and drywall cracks?
faqs.a: Katy's expansive clay soil swells and shrinks with rain and drought, and that movement shows up as nail pops, corner cracks, and separated caulk. We repair and texture-match these before painting so they don't telegraph through the new finish.

faqs.q: Is cabinet painting worth it in a Katy kitchen?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most Katy cabinet boxes are structurally sound and only need a new finish. A sprayed enamel over proper degreasing, sanding, and bonding primer updates the kitchen for a fraction of the cost and downtime of replacement.

faqs.q: What does your warranty cover in Katy?
faqs.a: Every Katy project is backed by our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty. The Standard 2-year package covers workmanship issues like peeling from improper prep or adhesion failure. The Premium 5-year package adds upgraded paint systems and prep for maximum long-term protection.

items.heading: Interior Painting
items.body: Most Katy interior calls start with flat builder-grade paint that scuffs, flashes at touch-ups, and won't wipe clean. We repaint walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and stair rails with a properly prepped, washable finish — including the tall great-room walls and two-story entries common in Cinco Ranch and Cane Island floor plans.

items.heading: Exterior Painting
items.body: Katy's brick-and-Hardie homes usually need trim, soffits, fascia, and siding repainted before the brick ever shows wear. South- and west-facing elevations fade and open at caulk joints first. We tell you honestly whether you need a full repaint or a targeted scope, and handle HOA color-approval paperwork.

items.heading: Cabinet Painting
items.body: Katy cabinet boxes are almost always solid — they just carry dated stain or a builder finish. Degreasing, sanding, bonding primer, and a sprayed cabinet enamel turn them into a custom-looking kitchen for a fraction of replacement cost, like the Cinco Ranch kitchen above.

items.heading: Drywall Repair
items.body: Settling on Fort Bend clay shows up as nail pops, corner cracks, and old patches that flash through paint. We repair and texture-match before we paint so the finished wall reads as one smooth surface.

items.heading: Fence Staining
items.body: Katy subdivisions run long stretches of cedar and pine privacy fence that gray out fast in open sun. We wash, repair, and apply a penetrating stain that soaks into the grain instead of a surface film that peels.

mechanismSection.heading: Why Katy Homes Wear Paint Faster Than Expected
mechanismSection.body: Katy sits on the expansive clay soils of the Katy Prairie, which swell when wet and shrink in drought. That movement is why nail pops, corner cracks, and separated caulk show up even in homes that are only a few years old. Outside, wide-open lots with young or limited tree canopy put heavy direct UV on south- and west-facing siding and trim, while Gulf Coast humidity pushes moisture into joints and end grain. Hard summer heat also stresses fresh coatings applied at the wrong time of day. We choose primers, caulks, and coatings, and schedule application around these conditions, instead of treating every surface the same.
